title: South Korea's FSC draft digital asset act would set a 10%-of-revenue fine cap for exchange hacks
date_note: Newsis (25 November) says the FSC held the Virtual Asset Committee meeting the previous day.
geo_basis: Financial Services Commission, South Korea's financial regulator, as stated by the source
summary: According to Newsis, the Financial Services Commission's draft digital asset act would impose financial-firm-level IT security duties on digital asset operators and allow punitive fines capped at 10% of revenue if a hack or IT incident follows a breach of them. A separate bill would raise the cap for financial firms to a cap of 3% of revenue. The draft also introduces no-fault liability for user losses.
plain: Newsis reports that a draft South Korean law would let regulators fine crypto exchanges as much as 10% of revenue after hacks caused by security failures, more than the 3% cap proposed for financial firms.
exec: Per Newsis, the FSC's draft would allow fines capped at 10% of revenue on digital asset operators for hacks tied to security failures, and no-fault liability for user losses.

validation.note: One publisher (Newsis) relaying the FSC committee meeting and briefing; FSC's own page not read.

evidence.quote: 이를 위반해 해킹이나 전산사고가 발생할 경우 매출액의 최대 10%까지 징벌적 과징금을 부과할 수 있도록 하는 내용이 담겼다.
과징금 상한을 현행 50억원에서 매출액의 최대 3%로 높이는 것이 핵심이다.
